Mahli
mä'lī
n. (elder son of Merari and head of the Mahlite family of Levites, who carried the boards, bars, pillars and sockets of the tabernacle)
From Hebrew Machli, connected with chalah, to be weak or sick — a name of no evident bearing on the man. Exodus 6:19 spells it Mahali; Numbers and Chronicles give Mahli.

Biblical Definition

Mahli is the firstborn of Merari, the third son of Levi, and the head of one of the two Merarite houses: “the sons of Merari; Mahli, and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to the house of their fathers” (Num 3:20), and again, “Of Merari was the family of the Mahlites, and the family of the Mushites” (Num 3:33). Their charge in the wilderness was the heaviest and least visible part of the tabernacle: not the ark and not the vessels, but the frame — the boards, the bars, the pillars, the sockets and the pins, all the ironmongery of a portable sanctuary. Because their burden was timber and bronze rather than holy things carried on the shoulder, they were given wagons: “four wagons and eight oxen he gave unto the sons of Merari, according unto their service, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest” (Num 7:8). The Mahlites appear again and again through the Chronicler's rolls, and once more at the very end of the Old Testament story: the man of understanding whom Ezra's messengers found at Casiphia, without whom the second return would have gone up with no Levites at all, was “of the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel” (Ezr 8:18).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Mahli; in sacred history he is the elder son of Merari, and head of the Mahlite family of Levites.

expand to see more

MAHLI, n. The first named son of Merari, the son of Levi.

In Exodus the name is written Mahali; elsewhere Mahli.

From him descended the family of the Mahlites, numbered among the Levites.

The Merarites had charge of the boards, bars, pillars and sockets of the tabernacle.

Sherebiah, who came to Ezra at the river Ahava, was of the sons of Mahli.

Key Scripture

Exo 6:19 — "And the sons of Merari; Mahali and Mushi: these are the families of Levi according to their generations."

Num 3:20 — "And the sons of Merari by their families; Mahli, and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to the house of their fathers."

Num 3:33 — "Of Merari was the family of the Mahlites, and the family of the Mushites: these are the families of Merari."

1Ch 23:21 — "The sons of Merari; Mahli, and Mushi. The sons of Mahli; Eleazar, and Kish."

Modern Corruption

There is no significant modern redefinition of this name. The principle to recover is that the unseen structural work of God's house is a divinely assigned ministry, not a lesser grade of one.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Mahli is the head of a Levitical family and nobody has contested him. What his house sets against the modern church is a doctrine of the unglamorous. Numbers assigns the Kohathites the ark, the table, the candlestick and the altars, borne on the shoulder and covered by the priests; the Gershonites take the curtains and hangings; and the Merarites — Mahli's house — take the frame. Boards, bars, pillars, sockets, pins and cords. Nobody looks at a socket. But the sanctuary does not stand without them, and God named the men who carried them and appointed wagons for the load.

The principle to recover is Paul's, argued at length precisely because congregations have always got it wrong: the parts of the body which seem to be more feeble are necessary, and God has tempered the body together, “giving more abundant honour to that part which lacked” (1Co 12:24). A church that honours only the visible gifts has adopted a doctrine of ministry the Pentateuch already refuted in its assignment of wagons. The man who keeps the building sound, the accounts straight and the doors open is doing the Merarite's work, and it was never the case that God valued the curtains above the sockets that held them up.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Machli (H4249), Mahli; Merari (H4847), Merari; qeresh (H7175), board, plank; 'eden (H134), socket, base; massa' (H4853), burden, load.

expand to see more

Hebrew Machli (H4249) — Mahli; elder son of Merari, head of the Mahlites.

Hebrew Merari (H4847) — Merari; the third son of Levi and his father.

Hebrew qeresh (H7175) — board, plank; part of the Merarite charge.

Hebrew 'eden (H134) — socket, base, foundation; the silver bases of the tabernacle frame.

Hebrew massa' (H4853) — burden, load; the technical word for a Levite's assigned carriage.

Usage

"“Of Merari was the family of the Mahlites” — a house defined by what it carried."

"“Four wagons and eight oxen… according unto their service” — the load measured, the help provided."

"“Of the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi” — the family still serving a thousand years later."
